preservation_method: fresh refrigerated vs stored in water glass

explain_adult: Hot smoking involves cooking fish to an internal temperature of at least 150°F, which in combination with refrigeration extends shelf life safely beyond that of fresh fish.
source_excerpt: Fish hot smoked to 150°F and refrigerated lasts 1-2 weeks; fresh fish lasts 1-2 days in fridge

preserved_shelf_life: 1-2 months room temperature; 3-6 months refrigerated; up to 1 year frozen
surprising_fact: Jerky can last several months unrefrigerated, a massive increase compared to raw meat’s couple of days.
safety_note: Store jerky in a cool, dark, dry place; check periodically for mold and discard if any is found.
explain_kids: Jerky is dried meat that keeps much longer than fresh meat because it has no water.
explain_tweens: Drying jerky removes moisture so bacteria can’t grow, letting it last months even without a fridge.
explain_teens: Jerky’s long shelf life results from moisture removal and curing, which inhibit microbial growth and spoilage.
explain_adult: Properly dried and cured jerky has significantly reduced water activity, preventing microbial proliferation and spoilage over months.
source_document: PNW 632 Making jerky at home safely
source_excerpt: Jerky keeps 1-2 months at room temperature, 3-6 months refrigerated, up to 1 year frozen

surprising_fact: Dried carrots last nearly a year, a stark improvement over fresh carrots’ two weeks.
safety_note: Store dried carrots in a sealed container away from light and moisture to maintain quality.
explain_kids: Drying carrots takes away water so they do not rot quickly like fresh carrots.
explain_tweens: Removing moisture from carrots helps stop them from spoiling for many months.
explain_teens: Dehydration reduces water activity, preventing microbial growth and thereby extending shelf life drastically.
explain_adult: Drying carrots lowers available water content, which in turn slows microbial and enzymatic spoilage, allowing long storage.
source_excerpt: Dried carrots keep 10-12 months; fresh carrots last ~1-2 weeks refrigerated

preserved_shelf_life: 2 weeks refrigerated smoked bacon, months frozen
surprising_fact: Smoking and curing bacon extends refrigerated storage from about a week fresh to two weeks and even longer if frozen.
safety_note: Cook bacon thoroughly and refrigerate; smoke alone does not ensure safety without temperature control.
explain_kids: Curing and smoking bacon helps keep it fresh longer but it still needs to stay in the fridge.
explain_tweens: Smoking and curing slows down bacteria on bacon, making it last longer than fresh pork belly.
explain_teens: Curing salts and smoking reduce microbes and spoilage, extending shelf life under refrigeration.
explain_adult: The combined curing and smoking processes reduce microbial load and enzymatic activity, allowing longer refrigerated storage than fresh pork.
source_excerpt: Smoked bacon keeps about 2 weeks refrigerated; fresh pork about 1 week
